Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-07-13 | AMZN | Underweight | +1.1% | +2.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim existing exposure to roughly 0.65x–0.75x of a standard benchmark allocation (a 25%–35% cut of intended weight), and do not initiate at $247.31 with price jammed under the $252–$254 confluence (falling 50-SMA $253.72, upper Bollinger $252.16) while MACD sits at −1.05, still below zero. Treat $252–$254 as a trimming/reassessment zone and re-entry trigger — not the "stop loss" the trader mislabeled, since a stop above spot is meaningless on a trim — and use a daily close below the rising 200-SMA at $233.47 as the hard trend-risk control that cuts AMZN to minimal or zero. Size so the $247.31-to-$233.47 distance (~$13.8, ~1.8x ATR of $7.56) fits the pre-set portfolio risk budget, and rebuild toward benchmark weight only on a decisive close above $252–$254 on above-average volume, or on a stabilized pullback into $237–$233.50 with Q2 evidence that capex is no longer consuming all operating cash flow. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk analysts converged on the direction — reduce, do not add — and the disagreement was only about degree, which is exactly the dispute this decision has to settle.

**What the bear side won decisively.** The tactical setup is unambiguous: AMZN closed at $247.31, below the falling 50-SMA at $253.72 and capped by the $252–$254 confluence where that 50-SMA meets the upper Bollinger band at $252.16; MACD has crossed its signal line but remains at −1.05, below zero; RSI at 52.9 is neutral, not a breakout reading. That is a repaired bounce, not a trend reassertion, and the aggressive analyst's point stands that waiting for confirmation above the zone means absorbing the full $13.8 (~1.8x ATR) distance down to the 200-SMA before the long-term trend even breaks. The fundamental overlay is equally specific: TTM free cash flow slightly negative (FY2025 FCF ~$7.7B, TTM ~−$2.5B), capex roughly 102% of operating cash flow (Q1 capex $44.2B against $26.0B OCF), long-term debt more than doubled to $122.6B with $53.4B issued in a single quarter and interest expense up 48%, operating leases of $91.6B, contractual obligations near $569B, and capex incurred but not paid at $27.0B. Q1 EPS of $2.78 was flattered by a $15.6B non-operating gain including a $12.3B non-cash revaluation — clean EPS is closer to ~$2.00, against a harsh YoY comp. That combination — paying up under resistance for a debt-funded capex cycle with no demonstrated return above cost of capital on a $151B TTM capex base — is what makes this a reduce, not a hold.

**What the bull side won, and why this is Underweight rather than Sell.** The conservative analyst is right that the primary trend is intact: price is above the rising 200-SMA at $233.47, the 50>200 golden cross is preserved, revenue grew 16.6% to $181.5B, operating income grew 29.6% to $23.85B with 130bps of margin expansion to 13.1%, TTM operating cash flow is $148.5B and liquidity is ~$144B. The aggressive analyst's framing of that as "static trend worship" overreaches — those are long-term trend facts, not near-term entry signals, but they do rule out exiting a franchise whose operating income is compounding at ~2x revenue. Equally, the trader's own "Sell" proposal is really a sizing call (trim to 0.5x–0.75x), not a risk-off exit. Underweight captures that precisely: reduce exposure, keep a core, take the optionality off the table, but do not abandon the position at a level still above a rising 200-SMA.

**Where I moderate both extremes.** I side with the conservative and neutral analysts against the aggressive analyst on the $25B data-center headline: it is a headline and a summary with no disclosed structure, pricing, or market reaction, against ~$144B of cash and securities — treating it as a near-certain bearish catalyst is a sentiment bet, not a risk read, and it should not drive size. Likewise the late-June 248M-share session could be accumulation rather than a dead-cat bounce, so I do not trim at the maximum 50% end of the range absent evidence the caller is tactically overweight. Conversely, I side with the neutral and aggressive analysts against the conservative analyst on sizing: a token 25% trim is too light when the caller may already be at or above benchmark, and the neutral resolution — trim 25%–35%, toward 0.65x–0.75x, with up to 50% only if tactically overweight — is the right calibration for an unknown book. I also adopt the neutral analyst's correction that a bare touch of $233.47 is not a buy signal; support must stabilize.

**Two process corrections.** First, the trader's stop at $254 is not a stop — it sits above spot. On a trim, $252–$254 is an upside invalidation and re-entry trigger; the real risk line is a daily close below $233.47. Second, prior AMZN work cut starters too small on short-window bounce objections (the 2026-07-06 Overweight earned +1.6% five-day alpha and the reflection rightly noted the entry-timing discount, not the thesis, was the marginal variable) — the reverse discipline applies here: the five-day alpha does not validate a FCF/leverage thesis, and the GOOGL lesson that "rebound, not trend-change" setups deserve zero positive momentum weight until a volume-backed close above the 50-SMA prints argues for trimming now rather than waiting for a $233–$237 retest.

**What would change the call.** Upgrade toward standard weight/Overweight on a decisive daily close above $252–$254 on sustained above-average volume, or a pullback into roughly $237–$233.50 that stabilizes with a reclaim; a fundamental upgrade additionally requires evidence capex is no longer absorbing all operating cash flow (incurred-but-unpaid capex falling from $27.0B), debt and interest growth stabilizing, and favorable disclosure of the $25B financing terms. Downgrade to Sell and cut to minimal/zero on a daily close below the 200-SMA at $233.47, which is the bull's own trend-invalidation line. Explicitly unresolved in this evidence set: the $25B financing terms, segment-level AWS/advertising margins, detailed contractual maturities, and the market's actual reaction to the funding headline — do not let any single headline move size.

**Price Target**: 237.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
Five-day alpha of +2.0% (raw +1.1%) went against the Underweight call, but the stated 3–6 month horizon means this window is too short to judge the FCF/leverage thesis that drove the rating. What it does undercut is the tactical premise — the "repaired bounce, not trend reassertion" read at $247.31 under the $252–$254 confluence — since price kept outperforming rather than failing at resistance, while the intact primary trend above the rising 200-SMA was the part the window supported. Lesson for next time: when the trend structure is intact and only the entry zone is adverse, size the trim toward the light end (0.75x) or wait for the $233.47 close-breach trigger instead of pre-positioning against momentum, since short-window alpha penalizes exactly that.

[2026-07-10 | AMZN | Underweight | +0.8% | +2.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: reduce to roughly 50–60% of a standard allocation (trim one-third to one-half of an at-benchmark position) rather than exit — the franchise is intact but the stock's near-term asymmetry, negative free cash flow and rising leverage all argue against carrying full weight at $245.34. Stage the trim: part into strength at $248–251 and $251–254, with the balance completed on a loss of $243 or a daily close below $237; put no new money to work at current levels. Keep a residual core with hard rules — halve again on a daily close below $237 and exit the residual below $227.01 — and re-add only in thirds on a high-volume daily close above $254 with MACD back above zero. Treat $254.5 as an upside reassessment level, not a tight bearish stop (it sits inside one ATR of ~7.7).

**Investment Thesis**: The debate splits cleanly along two questions and each side wins one of them, which is what makes this an Underweight trim rather than a Sell or a Hold.

The bull wins the ownership question, and all three risk analysts effectively concede it. Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 16.6% to $181.52B, operating income rose 29.6% to $23.85B, operating margin expanded ~130bps to 13.1% and gross margin ~120bps to 51.8%, on TTM operating cash flow of $148.5B, ~$144B of cash and securities, a current ratio near 1.18, and roughly $0.80B of quarterly interest expense against $23.85B of quarterly operating income. Price sits ~5% above a still-rising 200-SMA at $233.33, has reclaimed the 10-EMA at $243.05, and the MACD histogram has turned positive. That rules out Sell and rules out the aggressive analyst's framing of this as a high-conviction bearish bet: negative FCF at Amazon is a capex choice, not a solvency event, and the conservative analyst is right that a caller cannot assume a better opportunity exists to redeploy into when no portfolio context was supplied.

The bear wins the "at this price" question, which is the operative one. (1) Technical structure is unconfirmed, not repaired — price closed at $245.34 below a declining 50-SMA at $254.03, tagged the upper Bollinger band at $251.43 (intraday high $251.03) and closed near the session low on only 31.65M shares versus 248M on the 6/26 reversal (itself plausibly quad-witching/index flow, a distortion the neutral analyst correctly discounts). The MACD line at −1.523 remains below zero; a crossover inside a negative regime is a weak signal in either direction, so it does not license adding. (2) The asymmetry is poor: ~7.5% to the 227–229 shelf versus ~3.5% to the 50-SMA, with ATR at ~7.72 meaning one ordinary session can cover a third of the gap to support. (3) Fundamentals have a genuine quality problem — TTM FCF of −$2.47B against $151B TTM capex, quarterly capex at 1.85x quarterly operating income, long-term debt stepping from ~$68.4B to ~$121.9B in a single quarter with a record $53.4B issuance and interest expense +48% YoY, plus $91.62B of operating and $13.33B of finance lease liabilities. (4) Valuation leaves no cushion: roughly 34–36x core EPS after stripping the $12.3B non-cash private-equity mark-up, with the private-stakes book moving $16.2B to $48.1B in one quarter — a reversible valuation, not a durable earnings stream. Add the February 2026 gap (222.69 prior close to 202.70 open on 179M shares) as demonstrated catalyst risk.

On sizing and execution the analysts genuinely disagree, and I side with the neutral analyst's middle path against both extremes. The aggressive analyst wants the entire trim worked into the 251–254 band, which assumes a bounce arrives before risk can be cut; the conservative analyst wants to lean to the lower half of the residual immediately, which risks an over-trim while the 200-SMA and support shelf are still intact. The defensible compromise is a residual of ~50–60% of standard, trimmed in stages: into strength at $248–251 and $251–254, remainder on a loss of $243 or a daily close below $237. All three analysts agree on the guardrails — no new money at $245.34, halve the residual below $237, exit below $227.01, re-add in thirds only after a high-volume close above $254 — and on rejecting $254.5 as a tight short stop, since at ~7.72 ATR it is inside normal noise.

Prior-analysis lessons are applied directly: the last three AMZN calls (Overweight, then two Holds) all produced thin or negative five-day alpha because the actionable level sat ~5% away and the position was left at full weight against an unconfirmed tape. The fix here is to act on the asymmetry rather than wait for a trigger 3.5% lower, and to attach dated re-scoring checkpoints — next earnings print — plus an index-relative opportunity-cost check, rather than letting a trim drift.

What would change it: two consecutive high-volume daily closes above $254 with MACD above zero and RSI >55 convert this toward Overweight (staged re-add in thirds); TTM FCF back above zero or capex/operating-cash-flow trending down with D&A growth not outrunning operating income growth validates further add-back; any segment-level ROIC or AWS margin disclosure tying the $151B capex to identified returns would justify a full weight. Conversely, a daily close below $227.01 (June low, with the 200-SMA at $233.33 as the confluence above it) converts to Sell/exit, and evidence that the debt-funded capex cycle is impairing liquidity would force a flat position. Explicit evidence gaps that must not be priced in either direction: no segment-level ROIC or AWS/retail profitability split, no rating-agency data to support the "AAA-adjacent" claim, no insider-transaction data, a partial news sample, and a BofA target that is internally inconsistent ($165 against a ~$247 stock) and usable only as direction. Leo (396 pre-revenue satellites), Alexa+ agentic ads, European Sovereign Cloud and custom silicon remain unquantified options that justify holding a residual, not a full allocation.

**Price Target**: 254.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window produced +2.3% alpha, but that modestly contradicts rather than validates the Underweight call and is far too short to judge a 3–6 month sizing thesis. It supports the ownership argument — the franchise and 200-SMA held, so trimming rather than exiting was right — while undercutting the near-term asymmetry claim that risk outweighed ~3.5% upside to the 50-SMA. The lesson: when the thesis rests on poor asymmetry but the tape is unconfirmed, express it through staged sizing and dated re-scoring rather than a directional rating that a single benign week can falsify.

[2026-07-09 | AMZN | Underweight | +1.2% | +1.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Trim AMZN toward an underweight stance — sell a first tranche at market near 247.04, sizing to roughly 55–70% of a standard allocation, and place a second tranche at 250.83–254.32 only on a failed rejection of that band (limit orders, no chasing). Retain a core: the rising 200 SMA (233.24), intact golden cross, and price ~5.9% above it mean this is a valuation/cash-flow/setup problem, not a broken business. Stop the retained core at 233.24 (a daily close below cuts to the low end), treat 238.25 as a review trigger rather than an automatic cut (only ~1.1 ATR away), and re-upgrade in stages only on a decisive close above the 254.32 50 SMA that holds two to three sessions with MACD above zero. No naked short; horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate converged on trimming, so the decision was how far — and the shared bearish swing factors carried it. (1) Earnings quality: stripping the $12.3B non-operating stake revaluation from the $2.78 headline EPS leaves core EPS near $1.69, implying ~36x rather than the ~22x the headline advertises; this is decisive and undisputed. (2) Cash generation: FCF fell +$32.2B (FY23) → +$32.9B (FY24) → +$7.7B (FY25) → ~−$2.5B TTM, with capex ($151B) exceeding operating cash flow ($139.5B), plus $53.4B of new long-term debt in one quarter and a $25B concession-yield bond sale — the credit-leads-equity warning is fair even if the AI-buildout motive is legitimate. (3) Setup: at 247.04 AMZN sits beneath the 250.83 upper Bollinger and the declining 254.32 50 SMA with MACD below zero, roughly 2-to-1 against a fresh long — the strongest single argument. Why Underweight, not Sell: the operating engine is real (+16.6% revenue, +29.6% operating income, 13.1% margin, $139.5B OCF, ~$144B liquid assets), the 200 SMA is rising at 233.24, the golden cross is intact, and short-term tape is mixed-to-constructive (July 9 outside-up reversal, MACD bullish crossover, 248.4M-share capitulation volume, price holding the 236.95 VWMA). That rules out an exit or a naked short into a rising long-term trend. On the middle ground I side with the neutral analyst that 238.25 is ~1.1 ATR away and a mechanical cut there risks whipsaw at the 233.24 floor (review trigger, not automatic cut), and with the conservative analyst that the trim is risk reduction, not a 'win both directions' trade — re-upgrade requires a decisive close above 254.32 that holds two to three sessions with MACD above zero. Key gaps I will not paper over: no AWS segment revenue or segment operating margin is provided, so the bull cannot prove the profit engine is accelerating (this cuts against the bull), and there is no sentiment report and only partial news records. What would change the call: actual AWS revenue/margin, TTM FCF turning positive, long-term debt/interest stabilizing, or a confirmed reclaim of 254.32 — any material improvement argues for upgrading toward Hold/Overweight.

**Price Target**: 240.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The +1.3% alpha versus SPY over five days is mild evidence against the Underweight call, but five sessions are far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis or the 240 target. This window undercuts the setup argument specifically — the "roughly 2-to-1 against a fresh long" read at 247.04 beneath the 250.83 Bollinger and 254.32 50 SMA did not play out as resistance, though it says nothing yet about the core EPS-quality and FCF concerns that drove the rating. The lesson: when the bear case rests on fundamentals but the entry timing rests on a narrow technical band only ~1 ATR away, weight the trim sizing toward the lower end rather than treating near-term resistance as confirmation of the directional call.

**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Maintain the existing AMZN position at a standard (neutral) allocation and add zero at $243.62, where upside to the $250.37–$254.60 gate is only ~+2.8% to +4.5% against ~−7.4% downside to the $225.55 June low inside an elevated $7.70 ATR (~3.2%) — a poor entry despite a strong franchise (Q1 2026 revenue +16.6%, operating income +29.6%, margin 13.1%).
